card.name: Inside drug salt and ester names
card.fires_on: Pieces inside a drug's name just before its salt or ester ending, such as di- before acetate, hydrochloride or propionate. Seen mainly in drug labels.

modes.label: Di/tri prefix before salt
modes.description: The di-, dip-, tr- or dich- piece that comes right before a salt or ester word in a drug name.
modes.example: Diflorasone<< di>>acetate ointment should be applied

modes.label: Inside chemical names
modes.description: Hyphens or letters inside long systematic chemical names, or short pieces before bromide or butyrate.

card.writes: It favors completions of chemical-name endings such as chloride, hydro and azine.
card.plain: It marks the middle of a drug's full chemical name, where a salt or ester ending like diacetate or hydrochloride comes next.
